title: Review of c46's hunting ecology on fresh seed 9 (256^2): S, I, X and predator D replicate (prey 64 -> 4 -> 56 against a static 85-prey twin; 21 persistent predator splits, 23 strict); prey hardly divide (1 persistent, 0 strict) and the dividing kind's E is by construction
summary: labkit runs of the claimed world.py on seed 9: 256^2 with predators (rerun256, T=12000, --lineage-k 5), the predator-free twin (twin256), and at 128^2 the fuel fork at t=6000 (efork128) with its fed twin (fed128). With predators the prey go 64 (t=2000) -> 4 (t=3000) -> 56 (t=5000) -> 18-28 to t=12000 while predators hold 51-76; the twin is a static emulsion growing to 85 prey (21 slow prey splits, generation 1). Predators: 21 persistent splits, generation 2; the author's splits3.py finds 23 predator splits at area >= 8 (12 with no prey within 6 px, strict_pred8.png) and 5 at area >= 30. Prey: 1 persistent split, 0 by splits3.py. Fuel fork: prey 8 -> 0 by t=6900 against 5-7 in the fed twin; predators unchanged (27 vs 23).

observations.S: rerun256/sheet.png t=0 unstructured prey field; predators from noise added over the whole box at t=2000
observations.I: rerun256/sheet.png t=2600-12000: discrete predator droplets and prey condensates, separated by bath
observations.X: prey 64 -> 4 -> 56 -> 18-28 with predators (rerun256 metrics species n_comp) against twin256's static emulsion growing to 85 with no crash
observations.D: predators: 21 persistent splits, generation 2 (rerun256 FACTS); strict_pred8.png: rods and Y-shapes pinching into separate droplets, 12 of 23 away from prey. Prey: 1 persistent split, 0 strict, so D holds for the predator kind only
observations.E: prey bodies die after the fuel cut (efork128 8 -> 0 by t=6900, fed128 5-7), which is the prey's dynamical E; the dividing kind (predator) is made only from prey material, so for the individuals that divide E holds by construction

seeds_run.result: pass (S, I, X, predator D; E by construction for predators)

controls_run.X: twin256 (pred_on 0, same seed, grid, duration, window)

verdicts.limitation: The population dynamics show one predator-driven crash and recovery of the prey, then a slow decline, not repeated cycles; per RUBRIC L5 this is not a limit cycle without peak spacing on 3 seeds and a grid check. Prey reproduce by nucleation from the bath, not by division (1 persistent split), so 'populations that reproduce and eat' holds for predators only. The 128^2 fork has few prey (8) and the fed twin also loses prey to predators. The taxis toward prey is a written drift down the fuel gradient. One fresh seed; no dt/2.
